question_text: If x + iy = cis α · cis β, then find the value of x² + y².

mark_split.label: Combine cis α · cis β = cis(α + β) and read off x and y

recall_prompt: Say how you would find x² + y² — what the product of two cis values is, and what identity finishes it.
insider_note: cis α · cis β adds the angles in one line, and then x² + y² is cos² + sin² of the single angle α + β, which is 1. Expanding the two brackets term by term reaches the same 1 with four extra products and four chances for a sign slip.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Combine the cis product
steps.margin_note: First mark. cis θ means cos θ + i sin θ, and cis α · cis β = cis(α + β). Then x and y are the cos and sin of α + β.
lines: x + iy = cis α · cis β = cis(α + β)
x = cos(α + β),  y = sin(α + β)

recall.must_convey: That cis α times cis β is cis(α + β), so x = cos(α + β) and y = sin(α + β).
accept: cis alpha into cis beta is cis of alpha plus beta so x is cos of alpha plus beta and y is sin of alpha plus beta
the product of the cis values adds the angles, then compare parts
x equals cos alpha plus beta and y equals sin alpha plus beta
cis alpha cis beta ante cis alpha plus beta, real part cos, imaginary part sin
combine into cis of the sum and read off cos and sin

steps.why: Multiplying two cis values adds the angles — that is De Moivre's rule in its simplest form. It turns a product of four trigonometric terms into one angle, so x and y can be read off at once.
common_mistakes: Expanding (cos α + i sin α)(cos β + i sin β) term by term and losing a sign — correct but long.

steps.label: Square and add
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cos² + sin² of the same angle is 1.
lines: x² + y² = cos²(α + β) + sin²(α + β)

recall.must_convey: That x² + y² = cos²(α + β) + sin²(α + β) = 1.
accept: x squared plus y squared is cos squared plus sin squared of alpha plus beta which is one
square and add, cos squared plus sin squared equals one
square chesi add cheste cos square plus sin square, one vasthundi
x squared plus y squared equals one by the identity

steps.why: x² + y² is |x + iy|², and a cis value has modulus 1 — so the answer had to be 1 before any algebra. The identity is just the written form of that fact.
common_mistakes: Writing cos² α + sin² β and being unable to simplify.
Giving the answer as cos(α + β) + sin(α + β).
